title: Warranties and Consumer Rights
text:
A warranty is a written promise that a product will work correctly for a stated period. If the product fails during that time, the seller or manufacturer is generally obliged to repair it or replace it. However, most warranties exclude damage caused by misuse, accidents, or normal wear and tear. Consumers should therefore read the terms carefully before purchasing an item.

In many countries, consumer protection laws grant buyers additional rights that cannot be removed by a contract. For example, a shop may not refuse a refund for a faulty product simply because the warranty has expired. Nevertheless, enforcing these rights often requires keeping receipts and documenting the defect. Consumers who ignore these steps may find their claims difficult to prove.

questions.text: According to paragraph one, what must the seller or manufacturer generally do if a product fails during the warranty period?
options: Pay for the buyer's travel costs
Cancel the warranty for the buyer

questions.text: According to paragraph two, what do consumers often need to keep in order to enforce their rights?
options: Receipts and evidence of the defect
A written letter from a judge

questions.text: What can be inferred about warranties from the first paragraph?
options: They cover every possible type of damage
They usually do not cover misuse or accidents
They are only available for new products

questions.text: Why might a shop still be required to give a refund after a warranty has expired?
options: Because the law can grant rights that a contract cannot remove
Because warranties last forever in every country
Because shops must always accept returned items
Because receipts are no longer needed

paragraph_translations: Una garantía es una promesa escrita de que un producto funcionará correctamente durante un período determinado. Si el producto falla durante ese tiempo, el vendedor o el fabricante generalmente está obligado a repararlo o reemplazarlo. Sin embargo, la mayoría de las garantías excluyen los daños causados por mal uso, accidentes o el desgaste normal. Por lo tanto, los consumidores deben leer las condiciones con atención antes de comprar un artículo.

En muchos países, las leyes de protección al consumidor otorgan a los compradores derechos adicionales que no pueden eliminarse mediante un contrato. Por ejemplo, una tienda no puede negarse a reembolsar un producto defectuoso simplemente porque la garantía ha vencido. No obstante, hacer valer estos derechos a menudo requiere conservar los recibos y documentar el defecto. Los consumidores que ignoran estos pasos pueden encontrar que sus reclamaciones son difíciles de probar.
